# How we handle eBilling and A/R

eBilling and A/R consolidation is a planned service line, scheduled for months 12-30 of our growth plan, starting from an October 2026 baseline. The plan is to buy specialist billing providers and run four AI finance agents, priced on how quickly clients get paid (Frontline growth plan).

## Why law-firm billing needs attention

- Client-side AI now reviews invoices more aggressively.
- Invoice rejections have risen from 11% to 18% (Frontline growth plan).
- Each rejection means rework and slower cash for the firm.

## What the planned service looks like

- **Acquired expertise.** We plan to add billing specialists through acquisition. The screen includes Helm360, The Garver Group and The Legal Billing Group (Frontline growth plan). None of these deals is announced.
- **Four finance agents.** AI agents will handle eBilling and collections work. The context does not specify each agent's task.
- **Outcome pricing.** Fees will be tied to days-to-pay, not hours worked. When your cash arrives faster, we earn our fee.
- **International reach later.** Phase 4 (months 24-42) adds UK and Canadian providers, including Accurate Legal Billing (Frontline growth plan).

| Item | Planned approach | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Timing | Phase 3, months 12-30 | Frontline growth plan |
| Market trigger | Rejections 11% to 18% | Frontline growth plan |
| Build route | Acquire billing specialists | Frontline growth plan |
| Pricing basis | Days-to-pay | Frontline growth plan |

## What we cannot yet say

- We have no data here on current eBilling volumes, rejection rates by client, or days-to-pay baselines.
- A firm-level days-to-pay baseline and rejection history from pilot clients would show the likely improvement. We will not quote a number until that baseline exists.

Billing and A/R is where Frontline moves from IT support into its clients' cash flow. The growth plan counts on revenue-cycle add-ons for part of the roughly $25M of acquired revenue by month 24 (est.) and roughly $55M by month 36 (est.), so pricing on days-to-pay has to show up in EBITDA, not just in client goodwill (Frontline growth plan).

## Next actions

1. Pull current eBilling and A/R work from existing contracts across the 900+ law-firm clients to set a days-to-pay and rejection-rate baseline (Frontline growth plan).
2. Begin outreach and diligence with Helm360, The Garver Group and The Legal Billing Group ahead of the month-12 start.
3. Define what each of the four finance agents does, and draft days-to-pay pricing with a floor that protects margin.
4. Pick two or three AM Law clients with high rejection rates as design partners for a pilot.
